name: Silicone gel sheets

card.summary: Soft adhesive silicone patches worn over a scar to flatten it, soften it and fade its colour, so healed skin looks smoother.
card.aka: silicone scar sheets, silicone gel sheeting
card.note: Most studied on surgical and raised scars; effect on existing mature scars is smaller.

quick.overview:
Silicone gel sheets are thin, self-adhesive silicone pads placed over a healing scar. They are among the most widely studied non-surgical scar products and are used to reduce the height, stiffness and discolouration of scars such as surgical, hypertrophic and keloid scars.

The appearance payoff is a flatter, softer and paler scar. A 2020 systematic review of dermatologic studies found numerous high-quality randomised trials showing that silicone gel sheets and silicone gels significantly improved scar outcomes.
quick.how: The sheet is cut to size and worn over the closed, healed wound for many hours a day over months. It is washable and reusable in many brands. Topical silicone gel, which dries to a film, is an alternative with comparable results in a meta-analysis.
quick.risks: Reported problems are mild skin issues such as rash or irritation from prolonged adhesive contact. Patients with open wounds or infection are generally advised against covering them. Keloids and hypertrophic scars may need other treatments such as corticosteroid injections.

lead: Silicone gel sheets are soft, self-adhesive silicone pads applied to scars to improve how they look. A 2020 systematic review of topical scar products in Dermatologic Surgery, covering 34 trials, found that of 16 trials on silicone gel sheets, numerous high-quality randomised trials showed that silicone sheets and gels significantly improved scar outcomes, while few studies supported onion extract, vitamin E or microporous tape [1].

A meta-analysis of six randomised trials with 375 patients found topical silicone gel reduced scar pigmentation, height and pliability scores on the Vancouver Scar Scale compared with placebo or no treatment. Gel and sheet were comparably effective [2].

Wikipedia's article on hypertrophic scars notes that silicone gel sheets may improve scar appearance slightly compared with onion extract, and may reduce pain compared with no treatment or pressure garments [3].

chain: Sheet covers and hydrates the scar
angle.text: Worn over a healing scar, the sheet is used to flatten and soften it and reduce discolouration, so the mark is less visible on the skin.

paras: Used after surgery and injury to improve scar appearance. A randomised trial in people with normal healing studied linear scar reduction using the sheets [4], and a maxillofacial surgery series used the sheet as an adjunct in scar revision [5]. Reviews of keloid and scar revision list them among the least invasive modalities [6][7].

Trials in the 1990s compared sheets with steroid injection for sternal scars [8], tested silicone cream on scars and keloids [9], and used a sheet over donor-site wounds, where an antimicrobial-containing sheet was compared with collagen sheets and ointment gauze [10].

Meta-analytic results show reductions in pigmentation (SMD about -0.55), height (-0.73) and pliability (-0.49) for topical silicone gel [2]. A trial in children after catheter removal that used silicone patches found lower Vancouver scores than no skincare at 12 months, with no extra benefit from added corticosteroid cream [11]. A Cochrane review of pressure garments after burns examined a related approach [12].
Many randomised trials and meta-analyses exist. See the 2020 meta-analysis of six trials and 375 patients [2] and the systematic review of 34 trials [1].

timeline.event: Trials publish silicone gel sheet use on donor-site wounds and silicone oil cream on scars and keloids [10][9].
A randomised trial compares silicone gel sheets with steroid injection for hypertrophic sternal scars [8].
